title: About BharatVerse
text: BharatVerse is an AI-powered cultural tourism and local business discovery platform for India. It helps tourists and students discover states, cities, heritage sites, food, festivals and local artisans and vendors, with an AI cultural guide, a travel planner, a digital museum and gamified quizzes. The mission is Discover, Learn, Interact, Preserve.

title: Live information disclaimer
text: BharatVerse does not provide real-time prices, ticket costs, opening hours or availability. Visiting information shown in the app is demo content and should be verified locally before travelling.

title: Heritage places in Bihar
text: Bihar's most important heritage places include the Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya, where the Buddha attained enlightenment, and the ruins of Nalanda Mahavihara, an ancient university and UNESCO World Heritage Site. Bihar is the cradle of Buddhism and Jainism and was the seat of the Mauryan empire at Pataliputra (Patna).

title: Traditional food in Punjab
text: Traditional Punjabi food to try includes sarson da saag with makki di roti (mustard greens with cornbread), Amritsari kulcha with chole, tandoori dishes, and thick sweet lassi topped with cream. Punjab's food culture is hearty, dairy-rich and centred on hospitality.

title: Cultural places near Chandigarh
text: Near Chandigarh you can explore Nek Chand's Rock Garden, a sculpture park built from recycled waste, Sukhna Lake, and the Le Corbusier Capitol Complex. Chandigarh is a modernist planned city and the shared capital of Punjab and Haryana.

title: Forts and palaces of Rajasthan
text: Rajasthan is famous for hill forts and palaces including Amber Fort and Hawa Mahal in Jaipur, the City Palace of Udaipur on Lake Pichola, and the living golden fort of Jaisalmer in the Thar Desert. Several are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

title: Uttar Pradesh highlights
text: Uttar Pradesh is home to the Taj Mahal and Agra Fort in Agra, the spiritual ghats of Varanasi with the nightly Ganga aarti, and the Nawabi city of Lucknow with the Bara Imambara and chikankari embroidery.

title: Delhi heritage
text: Delhi has been built at least eight times and holds three UNESCO World Heritage Sites: the Red Fort, the Qutub Minar complex and Humayun's Tomb. Old Delhi's Chandni Chowk is famous for street food, while New Delhi has Lutyens' boulevards and India Gate.

title: Madhubani painting
text: Madhubani (Mithila) painting is a folk art of Bihar traditionally created by women using natural pigments, with densely filled surfaces and motifs of gods, fish, peacocks and nature. Styles include Bharni, Kachni, Godna and Tantrik.

title: Best time to visit North India
text: For most of North India — Rajasthan, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Delhi — the most comfortable travel season is roughly October to March, when temperatures are cooler. Summers can be very hot and monsoon months bring rain.
